mechanism_narrative: A persistently low federal funds rate (below 0.1%) compresses the risk-free rate, reducing the discount rate for equity valuations and generating positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS is below 0.1%.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly year-over-year CPI inflation rate exceeding 3.0% triggers a hawkish monetary policy response, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as investors anticipate rate hikes.
failure_condition: When CPIAUCSL YoY exceeds 3.0%, S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of instances.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in housing starts (HOUST) and rising unemployment (UNRATE) signal a weakening consumer demand environment, prompting equity investors to reduce risk exposure and generate negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint condition of HOUST decline and UNRATE rise fails to predict negative returns in more than 50% of cases (i.e., when both conditions are met, returns are positive in >50% of instances).

mechanism_narrative: During periods of strong economic expansion (GDPC1 growth above 2.5% annualized), consumer spending (RSAFS) growth exceeding 1.5% annually signals robust demand, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate earnings growth accelerates.
failure_condition: In periods when GDPC1 growth exceeds 2.5% annualized, RSAFS growth exceeds 1.5% annually, but S&P 500 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 4.0% signals a tight labor market, boosting consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when UNRATE is below 4.0%.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in industrial production (INDPRO) below 95.0 (index, 2017=100) indicates a contraction in manufacturing output, signaling economic slowdown and generating negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: When INDPRO falls below 95.0, S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of instances.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous weakness in industrial production (INDPRO < 95.0) and a persistently low federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS < 0.1%) indicate a stagflationary environment, where supply shocks are not offset by monetary policy, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint condition of INDPRO < 95.0 and FEDFUNDS < 0.1% fails to predict negative returns in more than 50% of cases (i.e., returns are positive in >50% of instances when both conditions hold).

mechanism_narrative: During periods of manufacturing expansion (INDPRO growth above 0.5% monthly), a concurrent increase in housing starts (HOUST) above 1,500,000 units signals strong consumer demand, generating positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: In periods when INDPRO growth exceeds 0.5% monthly, HOUST exceeds 1,500,000 units, but S&P 500 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of cases.
